title: Gravity and Colony Revisited
premise: Juniper Villalobos, a terraformer on the half-built colony of Meridian's Rest, tends a garden seeded for settlers who may never arrive while running supply routes between two worlds locked in a cold war her parents helped start. When she finds her mother's name — dead for fifteen years — on the manifest of a ship that officially never flew, Juniper is pulled into a conspiracy to deliver a sealed message that could end the war or shatter the fragile fleet truce. Pursued by both governments and haunted by what her mother actually did, she must choose between exposing the truth that would free the colonies and protecting the man she loves, a truce officer sworn to stop her. In the end she delivers the message at terrible personal cost: the war ends, but the garden — and the future it promised — belongs to someone new.
about_author: Paloma Winterbourne is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted greenhouse in the Pacific Northwest, where her novels are famously drafted among plants that refuse to die.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Juniper pilots a supply run between Meridian's Rest and the fleet station Halcyon Anchor, narrating the rhythms of a route no one else will fly since the embargo. She waters the colony garden by remote proxy and trades pleasantries with truce officer Elias Renn over comms. The beat is quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: On-planet, Juniper walks the terraformed terraces meant for colonists still in cryo-stasis, tending soil engineered for children not yet conceived. Her mentor Oyelaran warns her the funding council may scrap the project. The emotional beat is tenderness shadowed by futility.

chapters.title: A Name That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Auditing old manifests in the station archive, Juniper finds the freighter Vesperine listed as lost — with her mother Sera Villalobos listed aboard, fifteen years after Sera's official death. POV shifts briefly to Elias noticing Juniper's archive access flag. The beat is vertigo: grief reopened as a question.

chapters.title: What the Council Buried
chapters.summary: Juniper confronts Oyelaran, who admits the Vesperine carried an unauthorized diplomatic payload when it vanished — and that Sera was its courier. He begs her to let it go. The beat is betrayal by protection; Juniper refuses.

chapters.title: Truce Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Elias, bound by his oath to monitor anomalies, files a routine report he deliberately softens, buying Juniper time while compromising himself. Their growing intimacy sharpens the conflict between duty and feeling. The beat is complicity as courtship.

chapters.title: The Wreck That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Following debris-field records, Juniper locates the Vesperine intact inside a shielded asteroid drift, life support long dark but the cargo bay sealed. She boards alone. The beat is dread curdling into awe.

chapters.title: Sera's Voice
chapters.summary: In the wreck, Juniper recovers her mother's final log: Sera discovered both governments manufactured the war's inciting incident, and encoded proof in a message meant for the colonies' founding generation. The beat is a daughter meeting her mother as a stranger.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Lie
chapters.summary: Elias intercepts Juniper's return and must choose: arrest her or listen. He hears the log and realizes his own fleet command authored the original deception. The beat is faith breaking along institutional seams.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Fleet intelligence notices the softened report; investigator Captain Idris Vale arrives at Halcyon Anchor hunting the 'Vesperine anomaly.' Juniper goes dark, hiding in the station's hydroponics under a borrowed identity. The beat is hunted stillness.

chapters.title: The Garden Under Glass
chapters.summary: Hiding among the station's experimental crops, Juniper meets Toma Reyes, an aging botanist who once knew Sera and reveals the message was addressed not to governments but to the unborn colonists themselves — a letter of inheritance. The beat is unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: Deadline: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: Both sides' fleets begin repositioning as the truce clock runs down; Vale uses the tension to justify seizing all civilian traffic. Juniper calculates she has eleven days to deliver the message before the corridor closes. The beat is pressure becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Vale
chapters.summary: Vale offers Juniper amnesty for the message, but Toma recognizes Vale's name in Sera's logs as one of the original conspirators. The offer is a trap. The beat is temptation wearing an honest face.

chapters.title: Running the Corridor
chapters.summary: Juniper and Elias steal a decommissioned courier and run the embargoed corridor together, evading picket lines through a debris storm. Between maneuvers they finally speak plainly about what they want if they survive. The beat is love declared mid-crisis.

chapters.title: Meridian's Rest Lockdown
chapters.summary: They reach the colony to find it occupied by Vale's marines; the garden is being decommissioned as 'strategic biomass.' Oyelaran covers their entry at cost to himself. The beat is home turned hostile ground.

chapters.title: The Founders' Vault
chapters.summary: Sera's log points to a transmission array beneath the garden's root cellar, built by the first colonists for exactly this kind of truth. Juniper decodes the access ritual hidden in the planting cycles she has tended for years. The beat is inheritance fulfilled — her whole life was preparation.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Terraces
chapters.summary: Toma, revealed to have been reporting to Vale out of fear, gives up their location; Oyelaran is taken. Elias surrenders himself to draw marines away from the vault. The beat is sacrifice and guilt entwined.

chapters.title: Countdown to Silence
chapters.summary: Alone in the vault, Juniper begins the broadcast sequence as Vale arrives to shut it down; the truce expires in hours. She stalls him with the one weapon she has: the story of what the garden was for. The beat is defiance as persuasion.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: The message transmits fleet-wide: Sera's evidence, the founders' testimony, and the names of those who lit the war. Both armadas receive it simultaneously; crews mutiny against orders to fire. The beat is catharsis — truth as detonation.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Vale is arrested by his own officers; Elias faces tribunal for aiding Juniper and accepts it without regret. They part at gunpoint, neither sure they'll meet again. The beat is love paying duty's invoice.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: At the joint commission, Juniper testifies as courier and daughter, reading Sera's closing words aloud. The colonies vote to resume settlement and ratify a permanent accord. The beat is grief transmuted into legacy.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Months later, the first thawed colonists walk the terraces; Juniper hands the garden's keys to its intended heirs and takes a new assignment mapping routes between reconciled worlds. The beat is release — belonging achieved by letting go.

chapters.title: Gravity and Colony
chapters.summary: Elias, cleared and reassigned, appears at the head of a trade convoy on Juniper's new route; the book closes with the two of them flying side by side toward a world that finally speaks to its neighbors. The beat is quiet joy earned.
